title: The Soldier Who Fought For 29 Years After The War Ended
sources: Wikipedia: Hiroo Onoda — Imperial Japanese Army intelligence officer; stationed Lubang Island, Philippines 1944; surrendered March 9, 1974 after former commanding officer Yoshimi Taniguchi ordered him to stand down in person; last of the Japanese holdouts

BBC News / Time Magazine: Onoda fought for 29 years; killed at least 30 Filipino civilians and police in skirmishes believing war continued; returned to Japan a national hero; died January 16, 2014 aged 91

Hiroo Onoda, 'No Surrender: My Thirty-Year War' (1974 memoir): detailed account of jungle survival, guerrilla tactics, and refusal to believe surrender leaflets, newspapers, and family pleas were genuine
